text: {"standards":[{"code":"SL.6.1","verdict":"taught","reason":"The Part B and Part C fishbowl discussions have students engage in collaborative, teacher-led talk, building on peers' ideas while stating their own with evidence."},{"code":"SL.6.2","verdict":"taught","reason":"In Part C, students watch the film clips, record what they saw and heard, and explain how those choices change the scene and the topic."},{"code":"SL.6.6","verdict":"partly","reason":"The norms and discourse-marker practice ask for formal academic English in one discussion setting, but students never adapt their speech across different contexts or tasks."},{"code":"RL.6.7","verdict":"taught","reason":"Part C has students contrast what they saw and heard in the film clips with what they imagined or read in the novel scenes, as the standard describes."},{"code":"RL.6.9","verdict":"taught","reason":"Part B and the Part A Pulse Check have students compare how the myths and the novel, which are different genres, handle the shared themes of gods, heroes, and cultural messages."}],"anchorText":{"verdict":"uses","reason":"Part C has students watch 2-3 teacher-chosen movie clips from The Lightning Thief, matching the lesson text listed in the Outline."}}
